annotations.text:
COMPOSE · The wizard

Body first (the Instagram/YouTube spine): pick the body → crop → (cover, video only) → details → the seal; 'Write words instead' is the text path and skips crop and cover. The body is words OR what you show, never both. The pick screen: a PICKED TRAY on top (one line, 'Show all' on overflow) over the newest-first grid; the grid's first tile opens the device's own photos app, and picks made there land in the tray. THE CROP (Instagram's model): one shape for the whole post — Tall 4:5, Square 1:1, or Wide 1.91:1 — with drag-to-move and pinch-to-zoom per picture; 4:5 as the tallest shape is what guarantees the post ladder's height cap. Screens carry no step numbers (paths differ in length; the title names the stage, only the seal says 'Last step'). COPY RULE (2026-08-27): captions are one short line; the full explanation lives behind a small ? that opens a plain dialog — AT MOST ONE ? PER SCREEN, top-right of the header (or of the sheet/card it explains: the pads carry their own). It covers every compose explainer: cost and the community pool, the all-or-nothing batch, license terms and immutability, the stance side effects, the pending lifecycle, edit history. BUTTONS: filled and outlined pills carry 24px side padding and a 64px minimum width, so short labels (Next, Set, Done) keep their weight. The example everywhere: 1 post + 2 topics + 1 reference = 4 signed actions.

COMPOSE · The seal

'What you sign' is a place, not a popup — no 'don't ask again'. The manifest lists every act with its cost; the batch lands whole or not at all (resolves Q43). The three row-openers present ONE way (decided 2026-08-27): license and sensitive rise as BOTTOM SHEETS; the stance keeps the pad's own floating card, which is deliberately the same pad as everywhere else. License reads your default (a settings entry — new ruling), immutable after signing. Every stance the write signs is shown and adjustable: the post's own attachment is a ONE-AXIS pad (For/Against only — your own post always reaches you fully). Sensitive is one switch with a fixed per-field policy: it veils the BODY and the DESCRIPTION; the title and topics stay readable so choosing to look is informed. Optional reason, shown on the veil (new product decision — API field to add). Key absent = restore first: nothing staged, the draft stays on device, tertiary colouring — a waiting state, never error.

COMPOSE · Words, drafts, and after

The words body is the same wizard minus the cover step. Leaving mid-write keeps ONE local draft per target, on this device only — no discard confirm, the draft IS the safety. Signing exits to the post's own detail view: the post at top wearing 'Still settling' (its place in the feed comes as it settles), snackbar 'Signed — it's in the thread now, still settling.' If the act expires unlanded (Q38): a calm notice card in the shell — content left every reader's view, nothing was spent, the draft is saved. Never error colouring.

COMPOSE · Edit & remove the post

An edit is one screen and one batch (ruled 2026-08-27): the content edit PLUS topic and citation changes ride together — each add or withdrawal is its own priced act, the cost line reads the live total, and tapping it opens the breakdown sheet ('Edit · 1, Topic added · 1, Topic withdrawn · 1'), landing whole or not at all like every batch. License shown read-only with a lock. Earlier versions stay public under 'Edited'. Remove is the erasure path: own-post menu (a bottom sheet) → a think-twice dialog whose SAFE action is filled → the visible mark. 'Removed by its author' must never read like a moderation verdict — the two marks stay distinct. The thread and every response remain. Comment editing lives in the Comments rows above.

Citing — reached from Details. Searches everything citable: posts by title, people by name/handle, items by name, proposals by title, chats by name, campaigns by anchor, offers via their item. Comments and chat messages are cited from themselves — every content's overflow menu carries 'Cite in a new post'. These result rows are the seed of item 9's search.

COMPOSE · The post ladder — every container state in one place

From the smallest form (one line of words, nothing else) through bare media to the maximal collapsed container, plus the marked states: sensitive-veiled (blur + neutral wash + the author's reason; title and interaction row stay readable), removed by its author, and removed under the platform's rules — the two removal marks deliberately read differently.

THE HEIGHT RULE (2026-08-27): a post card's collapsed form never exceeds the screen height minus the bottom bar and the top safe zone — designed against the app / downloadable-webapp viewport, not browser chrome. Collapse order: the media and the interaction row NEVER shrink; tags and references collapse to one line under the description; the title clamps to one line; the description to two. The expanded detail view may be taller than the screen.

THE MEDIA SLICE (jakob 2026-08-31, for the product's media rebuild). The GALLERY IS A PAGER: every picture shares the post's one crop shape, swiped whole, dots only — never a '1/n' pill. Caps: 10 pictures or 1 video (+ its cover) per post; 4 pictures per comment. UPLOAD STARTS AFTER THE CROP — the crop happens on the device, only the cropped export is ever uploaded (the original can hold what the author never meant to share); comment pictures never crop, so they upload at pick. Progress rides the thumbnails as rings; a failed picture is marked on its tile with Retry · Remove beside it; the SEAL gates — signing waits for the pictures. DESCRIPTIONS (alt text) are authored, optional, never invented: entered per picture from the details step ('Describe the pictures · n of m described') and from the picked tray's Show all sheet — the per-picture manager (reorder, first = cover, remove, describe). Comment media is words-first: inset at the card's medium rung, capped at comment scale, same pager. Comment edit mirrors the post's one-screen-one-batch, license locked. Profile: ONE image — the avatar (no cover, per the ProfileHeader ruling); changing it is a SIGNED ACT with its own seal. Sensitive veils the WHOLE gallery, never one picture. Round 2 (jakob, same day): the details row carries NO Crop/Edit links ('none') — the row itself opens Show all; crop is one Back away — and the slice ships componentized (components/compose/: MediaThumb, PickedRow, DescribeCounter, PickedSheet, DescribeSheet, UploadStatusLine, UploadErrorLine, ActsCard), every board here rendered from the design system. Round 3 (implementation session's findings, same day): WEB has no device-gallery API, so 'Pick · the web variant' replaces the grid with the file picker + drop target — the rest of the step identical. The seal drift is healed in the component: ActsCard's note subline ('they land together, or none does') rides every MULTI-act seal's total; a single-act seal omits it. On the key-absent seal the ONE '?' belongs to the key notice (the 'Your key' dialog), not the header — one ? per screen, the key story outranks the seal story there. Off-role type values conformed to the pinned M3 roles (badge to label-small, writing bodies to 16/24, draft buttons to true padding) — M3 stays the default; no sub-roles added. Round 4 (jakob): THE WIZARD'S WAYS OUT — the header arrow steps ONE STAGE BACK, never out of the flow (Details reaches crop with it; the platform back gesture matches); the X leaves the whole flow from ANY stage, draft kept, NO confirmation (the draft prompt is the return surface); the seal's Back pill is the same one-stage step, labeled. WizardHeader is the master; every composer-flow stage wears the X, between the title and the trailing controls. The em-dash rule stands (asides keep their em dashes, per copy-voice). Round 5 (implementation session's findings, jakob's rulings 2026-08-31): COMMENTS HAVE NO PICK STAGE — '+ Add' opens the platform's own picker (Android's photo-picker sheet; the browser's file dialog on web), never the post wizard's grid; the one web addition is the drop path — files dropped anywhere on the composer are accepted, the quiet hint beside Add says so ('Reply · pictures on the web'). ALT TEXT IS DETACHED FROM THE UPLOAD (product ruling, recorded in api-spec/data-model): the upload moves bytes only; a description is witnessed in the act's manifest and rides the prepare input per placement — so comment pictures upload at pick, descriptions land at sign, NOTHING GATES on the other, and there is no alt-text-vs-upload race. The describe entry is the same counter line everywhere the composer shows picked pictures — the reply composer already wore it; Edit comment now does too. THE EDIT'S ACTS FOOTER OPENS A SHEET: 'This creates n signed actions' opens the M3 modal bottom sheet (the EditActs pattern — 'Edit comment · the acts' renders it with ActsCard; the sheet title carries the count, the card the rows and the all-or-nothing note). The sheet is the peek-from-a-composer pattern; ceremony screens keep the inline ActsCard — two patterns, one component. EditActs' pre-component note wording conformed to the ActsCard standard. Round 6 (jakob 2026-09-02 — comment video and the media error states): a comment carries four pictures OR one video with its cover, the post's grammar at comment caps, and the BYTE CAPS are product constants — a picture 10 MiB (10 per post, 4 per comment), a video 100 MiB in a post and 50 MiB in a comment, a cover 10 MiB. A FILE THE SURFACE REFUSES is refused where it was offered — 'Pick · files refused' here, 'Reply · files refused' on the Comments page — a line in the media row naming the cap it broke, never a dialog or snackbar, with Remove it as the only way out: a retry cannot shrink a file or fix its format. Caps are named ONLY in those lines, never in advance. MediaThumb grew the composer's video anatomy (play disc, duration) — authoring-side only, since a reading surface never draws play.

THE VIDEO CONFORM ROUND (jakob 2026-09-03, backlog item 32). What the video slice built to rulings without boards, drawn — and the two shipped mismatches ruled.

PLAYBACK STANDS AS DRAWN: sound only on every reading surface, both scales — no play/pause, no duration pill. Web strips its in-card transport controls; the real controls belong to the fullscreen viewer, which the roadmap now owns.

THE BACK ARROW GATES LIKE THE X: any leave of a non-empty comment asks through DiscardConfirm. Empty still leaves at once. Android's announced deviation is the rule; web adds the gate. Post composers keep their plain leave — a post draft is kept, so nothing is at stake.

REFUSALS, THE WHOLE VOCABULARY, on both refusal boards at their scales: the post video cap, the mixed-kind lines ('A post/comment carries pictures or one video, not both.'), the moving GIF (neither platform can encode animated WebP — a still GIF still converts), and count overflow, which used to truncate in silence. A FILE IS JUDGED ON ITS OWN BEFORE IT IS JUDGED AGAINST THE BODY: size and format first, grammar second — one file, one line, the nearest reason. Both boards stage a FULL tray, which is what makes the count and mixed-kind rows honest beside the rest.

MIXED SELECTION: staged content wins — the newcomer of the other kind refuses. From a fresh mixed batch with nothing staged, THE PICTURES ARE KEPT and the video refuses.

A VIDEO IS THE WHOLE BODY: once a clip is staged the add control is gone and a quiet line says why and what is next ('Pick · a video is the whole post'; the same at comment scale on 'Reply · a video and its cover'). Web takes the state 1:1 — the drop region and the file dialog play the grid's part, so no web board, the blessing ComposePickWeb's new refusal routes ride on too.

THE COVER: four frame samples — 1s, 10%, 50%, 90% — deduped on a clip short enough that two land on the same frame. A FRAME NEEDS NO CROP (it already carries the clip's shape); a picture from the gallery does, through 'Cover · a picture of your own', locked to the video's display shape at the scale it will be seen. ComposeCover's back arrow now reaches the pick, not the crop: the video path never crosses it.

THE COVER IS CHANGEABLE AT EDIT, VIA THE GALLERY ONLY — frames are not re-offered, because extraction needs a source file the device may no longer hold. A new cover is a NEW LAYER on the attachment: a new picture asset the author holds, the cover pointer swapping at edit-sign, never an alteration of the video. Both edit surfaces are drawn; the clip itself is never swapped, only removed whole.

A FAILED UPLOAD IS NOT A REFUSED FILE. Refusals are answers and cannot be retried; a failed upload is a fault and gets Retry beside Remove, like every other transport fault. Both apps ship no-Retry interims and must change.

THE DESCRIBE SHEET HAS TWO SHAPES: 'Describe the video' takes ONE entry for the whole clip and never offers the cover a field. Both shapes, and the describe row, carry the reason permanently under the title — 'Read aloud to people who can't see it.' — instead of behind a '?' nobody opens.

VERTICAL VIDEO IS RULED, ITS DRAWING DEFERRED: 9:16 and 16:9 both exist; square is the COMMENT scale's shape only. How the two sit in a feed card leads the next round (backlog item 33).

THE REEL ROUND (jakob 2026-09-03, backlog item 33, with his review-round rulings the same day). How a clip sits in a card, where a portrait clip's tap goes, and the stream it opens.

A CLIP KEEPS ITS OWN SHAPE, CLAMPED TO TALL. 16:9 and 1:1 display true; anything taller than 4:5 CENTRE-CROPS to 4:5 in a card. The cover shares the clip's ratio and crops identically — it is the same clip's face. LETTERBOXING EXISTS NOWHERE, pictures included: a tile is FILLED, never fitted, so a comment's uncropped picture display-crops to its square the way its clip does. Display only — the bytes stay the author's own, and the whole frame is one tap away in the viewer.

THE CONTROL LADDER — a deliberate revision of the conform round's sound-only-on-every-reading-surface rule. FEED CARD: the sound disc alone. DETAIL: play/pause and a real timeline, uniform for every clip; the chrome auto-hides and a tap on the video reveals it. FULLSCREEN VIEWER: the same full transport, and rotate-to-landscape. STREAM: sound and a thin drag-to-seek line — never the full transport.

THE TRANSPORT'S ANATOMY IS THE PLATFORM PLAYER'S: a big centred play/pause flanked by the skips, and a bar along the bottom with elapsed · timeline · total · sound · fullscreen. NOTHING SITS ON THE BOTTOM EDGE — Android's gesture zone lives there, and a control in it is a swipe that closes the app.

THE STREAM CARRIES PORTRAIT CLIPS ONLY, and it is THE DEFAULT FEED NARROWED TO THEM: same graph, same ranking, a mechanical filter. NO SECOND ALGORITHM, and no header saying so — what says it is the SCORE on the rail, the reader's own reach into this post, the same number the card wore. THE BOTTOM BAR STAYS (Instagram, TikTok and YouTube all keep theirs): the stream is a way of reading the feed, not a place outside the app. The seek line sits directly above the bar.

ENTRY: a portrait clip's tap in the feed opens the STREAM; any other media's tap opens the POST. From the pinned-clip detail, tapping the clip expands BACK to the stream with the reader's place held.

THE DETAIL DOOR IS THE SCORE ELEMENT — the exact element a feed card wears. Tapping it SQUISHES the clip to the top of the screen, still playing, and the body rises beneath: a state change, never a page portal. On a card the same element opens the score drill-down (item 13) — one element, two surfaces, two destinations, and no rename.

THE RAIL, top to bottom: author chip · stance face · comment count · share · the score. People lead; then the acts in the card's own order; the door out last, so a thumb reaching for the stance never passes over the exit. WHITE AND SHADOWED AT 28px, and the unset stance is a LINE FACE in the same weight (sentiment_neutral) — no disc, no ring, because a plate around one control in a column of five reads as chrome. Over photography a token colour is not a quiet control but an invisible one, so what the card says with translucency the stream says with the empty face; a stance already taken shows its own face at the same size. The stance opens THE SAME pad over the paused clip, seal and all; the count opens the same near-full-height comments sheet. Topics, references and the reader's ⋮ are NOT here — they belong to the detail view the score opens.

GUEST AND KEY-ABSENT GATE EXACTLY AS THE FEED: the join prompt over the paused clip, the key notice per the pattern boards. Same edges, same masters, no stream of their own.

SHARE IS NEW, AND IT IS ON EVERY CARD: one tap to the platform's own sheet, no menu of ours and NO COUNT — a share tally would be a public number the graph does not record. THE ACTION ROW'S ORDER IS ITS ORDER OF IMPORTANCE — stance · score · comment · share — and that is also the QUEUE: on a phone too narrow for all four, share moves into the ⋮ menu first, and the row gives way from its end. A new action is ranked against what is already reachable before it earns a slot, never appended by default.

THE COVER AT REST: first paint before autoplay, and it never returns once playback has started. Where the device suppresses autoplay — reduced motion, data saver — the card wears a PLAY DISC in the sound disc's place, the one card in the product that draws play, and a tap plays it where it stands. Quoted targets and history rows wear the cover as a thumbnail.

THE POST DETAIL EXISTS AT LAST, both bodies: the gallery post's, and the video post's with the clip pinned. The comments sheet's board is the first of these with the sheet raised — same anatomy, one screen.

THE FULLSCREEN VIEWER (jakob 2026-09-03, backlog item 33 — the surface the roadmap gave the real controls to, drawn).

IT IS THE WHOLE SURFACE, ON BLACK, WITH NOTHING BEHIND IT. Not a scrim over the post: a viewer you can still read a card through is not full screen, and the black ground is what makes the frame's own edges the only edges. Its stage is POSITIONED, never flex-sized — that is what keeps the frame, and the transport with it, inside the screen whatever shape the media is.

ENTRY IS THE SECOND TAP: media in a card opens the POST; media in the post opens the FRAME — or the transport's own fullscreen toggle, the same door. A reader scrolling is choosing between posts; a reader already on the post came to look.

THE FRAME IS NEVER CUT HERE. This is the surface every crop in the product exists against — the post's one crop shape, the 4:5 cap, a portrait clip's centre-crop — and here the frame is whole, as large as the screen allows. A clip whose shape is not the device's keeps its shape and takes the ground beside it; that is not a card letterboxing, it is the frame at its own size.

A PICTURE PINCH-ZOOMS, and the gallery's SWIPE AND DOTS carry over — the set pages here exactly as it does in the card: DOTS ONLY, no arrows and no n-of-m (the pager ruling holds here too; the count rides the accessible name).

A VIDEO TAKES THE FULL TRANSPORT — the centred play/pause and its skips, and the bar of elapsed · timeline · total · sound, INSET from the bottom edge and clear of the system gesture zone — the product's own, not the browser's default set, so one control vocabulary runs across the detail view, the stream and here. ROTATING THE DEVICE gives the clip the screen's whole height (Viewer · rotated, the one board in this canvas that is not a portrait phone). Rotation is the device's gesture, so nothing draws a rotate control.

THREE WAYS OUT: the X, a SWIPE DOWN, and the backdrop. An X rather than a back arrow — a layer is being dismissed, not a step of a journey walked.

NO ACTS: no stance, no comment count, no share. Acting on a post happens where the post is, and a viewer that grows a toolbar is a viewer nobody trusts to close.

THE DESCRIPTION IS NOT SHOWN. Alt text is read aloud to people who cannot see the frame; printed under it, it becomes a caption its author never wrote.

THE VIDEO-COVER ROUND (jakob 2026-09-10, backlog item 49). Three rulings about the still a clip wears, and the wizard they rewrite.

THE COVER'S CROP IS IN THE WIZARD, BOTH PLATFORMS. Every GALLERY-sourced cover passes the locked crop at the clip's ratio before upload; a FRAME needs none, because it was cut from the clip and already carries its shape. Only the cropped export ever leaves the device — the same principle pictures follow, and the reason is the same: the original frame can hold what the author never meant to share. Web takes the cover step and its crop 1:1, the file dialog playing the picker's part — the avatar flow's blessing again, so no web board.

THE 4:5 CLAMP STANDS, CONFIRMED: 'taller than 4:5 is reserved for the reel scroller.' Feed · the clip's three shapes holds the three presentations against each other — 16:9 TRUE, 1:1 TRUE, 9:16 CENTRE-CROPPED to 4:5, filled and never letterboxed. It is a reference board for the reason the cover-at-rest board is not: three whole video cards do not fit a phone, and a feed shows one at a time.

NO COVER IS FIRST-CLASS, AND THE DEFAULT IS SHAPE-KEYED. A VERTICAL clip defaults to NO cover: the cover step is skipped and what it would have been is one optional 'Add a cover' door on details. Horizontal and square clips keep the frame picker. SHAPE ALONE DECIDES, NEVER LENGTH. Why: an autoplaying video that has a cover LOOKS BROKEN — the cover flashes for an instant before playback takes it away — and a short-vertical author must not meet a step they were always going to skip. 'Videos are always moving, never at rest.'

WHAT A COVERLESS CLIP WEARS is its FIRST FRAME, cropped exactly as the clip is: the suppressed-autoplay card shows it under the play disc, and quoted targets and history rows take it as their thumbnail. Nothing on a reading surface branches on it — a still is a still, and which one it is was settled while the post was written.

WHEN EXTRACTION FAILS (Cover · no frames came back) the step shrinks to the one path that still works: the gallery tile alone, under a line saying why, over the NEUTRAL TILE — no frame is no picture, and the rule against inventing imagery is not suspended by an error. Next stays live: a post can always go without a cover.

COMMENT SCALE INHERITS at its scale. There is no step to skip in a one-screen composer, so the cover ROW is what gives way: a vertical clip's reply shows the door, and the row is what the door opens. The post edit does the same — a vertical clip's edit offers 'Add a cover' and never a cover row presuming one exists.
